title: DKA 3 of 7, step-down / telemetry: type 1 diabetes in DKA after months of cost-related insulin rationing (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: Diabetic ketoacidosis with severe biochemical features (glucose 684, pH 7.23, bicarbonate 9, anion gap 27, BHB 7.2) in type 1 diabetes after 3 months of stretching insulin she could not afford; prerenal AKI; low potassium (3.2) with insulin held on Day 1 morning and replaced by peripheral piggybacks; low phosphate monitored; low glucose after a fixed meal dose with a small lunch; discharge with medicines and supplies in hand
desc: Mon 11/09 0700 to Thu 11/12 0700. A 38-year-old single mother lost her job and insurance, stretched glargine to every other night and skipped meal insulin, then vomited for two days and arrived in DKA. Adult protocol (insulin 6 units/h, no bolus; peripheral IVs only so no more than 10 mEq/h of potassium from all sources): K falls to 3.2 at 0800 and the insulin is held for 2 hours while four KCl piggybacks and magnesium run, then restarts; dextrose and 3 units/h at glucose 220; resolution at 1545 (BHB 0.4); glargine two hours before the drip stops. A low after a fixed meal dose with a small lunch, a pen mix-up in the teach-back, and the real work: social work, pharmacy, case management, a food plan and supplies physically in hand before discharge. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
